Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/project-git

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

9	/-!
10	# The `HasRigidPushforward` gate, factored into its exact remaining leaves
11	
12	`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` declares the campaign gate
13	`Scheme.HasRigidPushforward C` (:373) with two fields, `locallyFree` and
14	`baseChange`, and no instance anywhere in the tree.  The purpose of this file
15	is to make the *shape* of the discharge exact: to say, as machine-checked Lean
16	rather than prose, precisely which statements remain and how they compose into
17	the gate.
18	
19	## The factorization
20	
21	For an AJC curve — `C : Over (Spec k)` with
22	`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`
23	— the gate is *equivalent* to four named statements, three of which concern
24	only `ℙ¹`:
25	
26	1. **`IsIntegral (ℙ¹_k)`** (`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Constants.lean` §5):
27	   integrality of the projective line over the one field `k`.  This is the
28	   sharpest sufficient form of the `H⁰`-finiteness anchor; the stronger
29	   `Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k` (`P1HasTrivialConstants k`, §3 there) and the still
30	   stronger `GeometricallyIntegral (p1Over k).hom` both imply it and both
31	   also discharge the anchor, through `p1RigidPushforwardStatement_of_leaves`.
32	2. **`P1CechFibrewiseBridge k A`** (§1 here): fibrewise `Ȟ¹`-vanishing of `M`
33	   on `ℙ¹_A` at all scheme points forces the base-linear Čech differential to
34	   stay surjective after `⊗ κ(𝔪)` at maximal ideals.  This is the geometric
35	   half of Mumford's "vanishing on the closed fibres" hypothesis, in the
36	   spelling the algebraic engine consumes.
37	3. **`P1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge k A`** (§2 here): the *output* bridge —
38	   the engine's module-level conclusion (`d` surjective, `H⁰ = ker d` finite
39	   projective, `H⁰` commuting with arbitrary base change) upgraded to the
40	   sheaf-level conclusion that `p_* M` is locally free of pointwise rank
41	   `p.fiberH0 M t`.
42	4. **`Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange C A`** — the second gate field, for
43	   which the tree currently has *no* infrastructure at all (see the caveat
44	   below).
45	
46	§3 assembles 1–3 into `P1RigidPushforwardStatement k A`, the sole hypothesis
47	of `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1Engine`
48	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`:1391), hence into the gate's
49	`locallyFree` field; §4 assembles everything into `HasRigidPushforward C`.
50	Note that `HasFiniteMapToP1 C`, which the transfer package needs, is **not** a
51	leaf: it synthesizes for an AJC curve through
52	`hasFiniteMapToP1_of_existsNonconstantMapToP1` ∘
53	`existsNonconstantMapToP1_of_existsNonconstantMapToProjInt` ∘
54	`existsNonconstantMapToProjInt_of_ajc`
55	(`RiemannRoch/Adelic/{FiniteMapToP1,NonconstantToP1}.lean`), all sorry-free.
56	
57	## Caveat on the `baseChange` field (recorded, not hidden)
58	
59	`Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` asks for `IsIso` of the adjoint mate
60	`pushforwardBaseChangeMap` for the **proper** family `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` and
61	*arbitrary* ring maps `A → A'`.  The tree's only `IsIso` theorems for that
62	mate (`isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback`,
63	`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`:1108, and its chart form :949) require
64	`[IsAffineHom f]`, and with `IsAffineHom q` assumed the field closes in one
65	line — so the entire content of the field is the non-affine case.  There is
66	also no composition/pasting API for `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` in the tree, so
67	the natural "reduce along the finite `π_A`, then treat `p : ℙ¹_A ⟶ Spec A`"
68	strategy cannot yet be assembled even once the second half exists.  The
69	module-level input is available (`kerBaseChange` bijective for *every*
70	`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`-algebra, the fourth conclusion of
71	`p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing`); the sheaf-level bridge is
72	not.  This is deliberately left as the fourth leaf rather than papered over.
73	
74	Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5; EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
75	12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5; Stacks 02KG.
76	-/

92	/-! ## §1. Leaf 2 — the fibrewise Čech bridge on `ℙ¹_A`
93	
94	The engine `p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing`
95	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Engine.lean`:1198) runs Nakayama over the maximal
96	ideals of `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`, so it needs `H¹` vanishing in the form
97	"`d ⊗ (R₀ ⧸ 𝔪)` is surjective".  `P1RigidPushforwardStatement` supplies `H¹`
98	vanishing in the *geometric* form `Hom.FiberH1Vanishing` — vanishing of the
99	concrete Čech `Ȟ¹` of `M_t` on *some* 2-affine cover of the scheme-theoretic
100	fibre `ℙ¹_t`, at *every* scheme point `t`.  This `Prop` is exactly the
101	implication between the two. -/
102	
103	/-- **Leaf 2 (the fibrewise bridge)**: on `ℙ¹_A`, fibrewise Čech
104	`h¹`-vanishing of a finitely presented `M` at every scheme point implies that
105	the base-linear Čech difference map of the standard 2-chart cover stays
106	surjective after tensoring with the residue field `R₀ ⧸ 𝔪` of every maximal
107	ideal.
108	
109	Both directions of the mismatch are favourable: the hypothesis ranges over
110	*all* scheme points while the conclusion needs only the closed ones, and
111	cover-independence of the fibrewise `Ȟ¹` is already unconditional
112	(`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing.surjective_moduleSectionDiff`,
113	`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/QuasicoherentDegreeOneVanishing.lean`).
114	What remains is the chart-level base-change identification
115	`κ(t) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(M, U_i) ≅ Γ(M_t, U_i^t)`, i.e. Stacks 02KG in
116	degree `0` on each affine chart of `ℙ¹_A`. -/
117	def P1CechFibrewiseBridge (k : Type u) [Field k]
118	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
119	  ∀ (M : (Limits.pullback (p1Over k).hom
120	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules),
121	    M.IsFinitePresentation →
122	    (∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
123	      (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
124	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing M t) →
125	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
126	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
127	        (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₁
128	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
129	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
130	        (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₂
131	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
132	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
133	        ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₁ ⊓ (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₂)
134	    ∀ (m : Ideal Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)), m.IsMaximal →
135	      Function.Surjective
136	        (((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).moduleSectionDiffBase
137	          (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
138	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M).baseChange
139	          (Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) ⧸ m))

141	/-! ## §2. Leaf 3 — the output bridge (module conclusion ⟹ sheaf conclusion)
142	
143	`p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing` ends at the level of
144	`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`-modules: `H⁰ = ker d` is finite projective and its formation
145	commutes with arbitrary base change.  `P1RigidPushforwardStatement` asks
146	instead for the *sheaf* `p_* M` on `Spec A` to be locally free with the
147	pointwise rank `p.fiberH0 M t`.  The two are connected by
148	`AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`
149	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Engine.lean`:287, `Γ(ℙ¹_A, M) ≃ₗ ker d`),
150	quasi-coherence of the pushforward (`pushforward_isQuasicoherent`,
151	`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`) and the standard "finite projective localizes to
152	free" argument; the rank identification is the `B = κ(t)` case of the
153	base-change conclusion. -/
154	
155	/-- **Leaf 3 (the output bridge)**: on `ℙ¹_A`, the engine's module-level
156	conclusion for a finitely presented `M` — the base-linear Čech differential
157	`d` surjective, `H⁰ = ker d` a finite projective `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`-module, and
158	the formation of `H⁰` commuting with arbitrary base change — implies the
159	geometric conclusion of `P1RigidPushforwardStatement`: every `t : Spec A` has
160	an open neighbourhood on which `p_* M` is free of rank `p.fiberH0 M t`.
161	
162	This is pure sheaf-theoretic packaging (no new cohomology): `Γ(Spec A, p_* M)`
163	is `Γ(ℙ¹_A, M) ≅ ker d`, the pushforward is quasi-coherent, a finite
164	projective module over a commutative ring becomes free on a basic open
165	neighbourhood of any prime, and the rank there is the `κ(t)`-dimension of
166	`κ(t) ⊗ ker d ≅ ker (d ⊗ κ(t)) = Γ(ℙ¹_t, M_t)`, i.e. `p.fiberH0 M t`. -/
167	def P1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge (k : Type u) [Field k]
168	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
169	  ∀ (M : (Limits.pullback (p1Over k).hom
170	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules),
171	    M.IsFinitePresentation →
172	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
173	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
174	        (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₁
175	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
176	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
177	        (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₂
178	    letI := (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
179	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).baseSectionsModule M
180	        ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₁ ⊓ (p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).U₂)
181	    Function.Surjective ⇑((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).moduleSectionDiffBase
182	        (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
183	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M) →
184	    Module.Finite Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
185	      (LinearMap.ker ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).moduleSectionDiffBase
186	        (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
187	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M)) →
188	    Module.Projective Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
189	      (LinearMap.ker ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).moduleSectionDiffBase
190	        (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
191	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M)) →
192	    (∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) B],
193	      Function.Bijective (AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange
194	        ((p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).moduleSectionDiffBase
195	          (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
196	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))) M) B)) →
197	    ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
198	      ∃ U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens, t ∈ U ∧
199	        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj
200	            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
201	              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj M) ≅
202	          _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
203	            (ULift.{u} (Fin ((pullback.snd (p1Over k).hom
204	              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 M t))))

278	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]

11	# The `HasRigidPushforward` frontier after the fibre-chart and sheaf bricks
12	
13	`Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean` factored the B3 campaign gate into four

15	the resulting state of the frontier — as Lean, not as prose.

17	## What is now closed
18	
19	* **Leaf 2, `P1CechFibrewiseBridge k A`, is PROVED**
20	  (`p1CechFibrewiseBridge_proved` below, from
21	  `Adelic.p1_hfib_of_fiberH1Vanishing`,

23	  `h¹`-vanishing of a finitely presented `M` on `ℙ¹_A` at every scheme point
24	  really does force the base-linear Čech differential to stay surjective
25	  after `⊗ κ(𝔪)` at every maximal ideal.  The proof runs Stacks 02KG in
26	  degree `0` on each affine chart of `ℙ¹_A` — the section-ring pushout on
27	  arbitrary compatible affine opens (`isPushout_appLE_of_isPullback'`,
28	  generalising the `f ⁻¹ᵁ V`-pinned form, which is unusable here because
29	  `p ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ = ℙ¹_A` is not affine), the resulting chart comparison
30	  `κ(t) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(M, W) ≅ Γ(M_t, W_t)` and its restriction
31	  naturality, the intertwining with the Čech differential, and the
32	  maximal-ideal-to-point package.
33	
34	* **Leaf 3's sheaf half is PROVED**
35	  (`Adelic.p1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge_of_rank`,
36	  `Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean`): a quasi-coherent module on
37	  `Spec R` whose global sections are finite projective *is* free of rank
38	  `rankAtStalk` on a basic-open neighbourhood of any point
39	  (`exists_free_restrict_of_finite_projective_sections`), and
40	  `Γ(Spec A, p_* M)` really is `ker d`
41	  (`Adelic.pushforwardTop_linearEquiv_ker`).
